thread:
maria: Pushed a docs PR to update the model catalog entries for 'redwood/ceres-7b' and its quantized variants — adds supported runtimes, sequence limits, and a small benchmark. PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/482

ton y: Reading. quick q: did you include the exact CUDA/ROCm compatibility? Some customers hit mismatch on ROCm 5.6

maria: Not in detail yet. I added a short note 'Linux + CUDA 11.8, ROCm 5.x supported' but we should list tested driver versions and exact kernels

sarah: I'd prefer listing tested configs like 'Ubuntu 22.04, CUDA 11.8 (driver 525.85), ROCm 5.6' and separate rows for A100 vs V100. Also include perf numbers for seq=512 and seq=2048

leo: Also add recommended quantization guidance: use q4_0 for lowest latency, q8_0 if you need better fp16 parity. Example CLI to demo serving: 
```bash
rw-serve --model redwood/ceres-7b-q4 --gpus 1 --batch 8
```

ajay: A short SDK snippet showing the canonical model alias would help — a lot of users call 'ceres-7b' but hosted alias is 'redwood/ceres-7b-v1'

maria: +1. I'll update the PR body & add a migration note: 'if you relied on the old alias `ceres-7b` -> switch to `redwood/ceres-7b-v1` or use the model_alias mapping in your SDK'

docs-bot: Reminder: docs PR template requires a filled 'backwards compatibility' and 'benchmarks' sections :robot_face:

tony: tagging @sarah @leo for review on the compatibility table. If you can add driver/test matrix and a short note on memory footprint for 8k context that'd be great :eyes:

sarah: I can add memory footprint numbers. Do we have PEFT/LoRA compatibility tested? Might need a separate subsection for adapter workflows

leo: We tested PEFT with fp16, but quantized q4 models need adapters hosted on CPU — add a short note: 'PEFT supported; for q4 quantized models place adapters on CPU (adapter-in-CPU) to avoid CUDA mismatch'

maria: Cool. I'll push changes tonight. Can reviewers try to land by EOD tomorrow? If not, I'll flag in the release notes for the next docs deploy

ajay: FYI: support ticket #3421 mentioned a tokenizer mismatch for 'ceres-7b' — probably the old tokenizer config. Add canonical tokenizer id `redwood/ceres-7b-tokenizer-v1` and a sample fix in SDK

tony: Good catch. Also add a brief compatibility matrix link: https://redwood.inference.internal/model-compat (internal)

maria: Added SDK example and migration snippet. Python snippet included: 
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client()
resp = client.generate(model='redwood/ceres-7b-v1', prompt='Summarize...')
print(resp.text)
```

sarah: LGTM apart from a tiny typo in the q4 note. I'll approve after that fix :thumbsup:

leo: I'm fine to merge once CI passes. docs-bot: can you kick CI for this PR?

docs-bot: CI queued for docs PR #482 — status will be posted here when ready

maria: Thanks all — pushed the fixes and added a small benchmark table (p50/p95 latency for seq512 and seq2048 on A100-80GB). PTAL: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/482

ajay: One more nit: please call out that batch sizes in hosted env use auto-batching and the recommended client batch is 4-8 for low tail latency

tony: Also, add a short note under 'limits' about max context: 8192 tokens for ceres-7b-v1, and that longer contexts are experimental and may be truncated

maria: Done. Thanks everyone — will merge after CI and then backfill a short migration blurb in the release notes. If anyone sees anything else, comment on the PR.
